predecessors.name: Northern Zhou
predecessors.text: the Northern Zhou realm, which Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou handed to Yang Jian on 4 March 581

predecessors.name: Later Western Liang
predecessors.text: Jiangling and the Western Liang territory in central Hubei

predecessors.name: Chen dynasty
predecessors.text: the Chen realm south of the Yangtze, taken in 589

successors.name: Tang dynasty
successors.text: Chang'an, taken by Li Yuan in winter 617, and the Tang founded there in 618; the Tang then took most of the Sui empire from the rival regimes by 628

successors.name: Wang Shichong's Zheng
successors.text: Luoyang, where Yang Tong's Sui yielded to Wang Shichong in summer 619

ledger.x: 581: Yang Jian ascends as Emperor Wen of Sui at Daxing.
581: the Western Liang passes to the Sui's protection.
587: the Sui ends the Western Liang's puppet status by abolishing it (see the gain below).
587: the Sui abolishes the Western Liang.
588: the Sui offensive on the Chen.
589: Jiankang falls.
589: the Sui reunify China.
600: the Sui backs the Qimin Khan of the Eastern Turks.
602: Sui retakes the Hanoi area.
605: the court moves from Daxing to Luoyang.
608: the Sui seize the Tuyuhun lands.
609: the Western Regions come to Zhangye.
612: the Sui army crosses the Liao River against Goguryeo.
614: the war ends with no Sui gain.
615: the Turks turn on the Sui.
617: Li Mi holds Henan as Duke of Wei.
617: Liang Shidu holds the Ordos.
617: Liu Wuzhou holds northern Shanxi.
617: Gao Kaidao holds northern Hebei.
617: Dou Jiande holds the Hebei plain.
617: Xue Ju holds eastern Gansu and western Shaanxi.
617: Xiao Xian rises at Baling.
617: Lin Shihong holds Jiangxi and Guangdong.
617: Li Yuan takes Chang'an.
617: the Tuyuhun commanderies lapse.
618: Xiao Xian takes the middle Yangtze and the south.
618: the Western Regions' tributary tint ends with the Sui court; the pages opened date no end.
618: Emperor Yang is assassinated and the empire breaks up.
618: Wang Shichong crushes Li Mi and Li Mi's land comes over to the Luoyang court.
619: the last Sui regime yields to Wang Shichong.

wars.name: Sui conquest of the Chen
wars.outcome: Sui victory: Jiankang taken in spring 589 and the last Chen emperor captured; the south joins the Sui.

wars.name: Goguryeo-Sui War
wars.outcome: Goguryeo victory; Sui withdrew in 614 holding no Goguryeo land and the losses 'contributed to the fall of the Sui dynasty'.

wars.name: Linyi-Champa Campaign
wars.outcome: Sui retook the Hanoi area in 602 and won a battle against Cham war elephants, but 'many soldiers died of disease'.

wars.name: Sui conquest of the Tuyuhun
wars.outcome: Sui victory: Murong Fuyun fled and the Sui set up four commanderies; Emperor Yang toured the land in spring 609.

wars.name: Sui and the Turkic Khaganate
wars.outcome: The Sui split the Turkic Khaganate into Eastern and Western halves by diplomacy, protected the Qimin Khan in 600 and was attacked by Shibi Khan at Yanmen in 615.

wars.name: Sui rebellions and the Transition from Sui to Tang
wars.outcome: The Sui court fell in 618-619; the Tang beat the Xue, Liu, Wang, Dou, Xiao, Gao and Liang regimes between 618 and 628.

certainty.note: Frontiers with the steppe, Tarim, Tibetan plateau and Goguryeo are approximate; the Yangtze line to the Chen (581-588) and the 602 Red River frontier are the firmest edges but no treaty or survey fixes them; rebel-held land after 616 is…
